status: Specification only. No model has been fitted, no coefficient exists, and no probability is published. Every numeric field below that would be an estimate is null by design.

origination_order.rule: Originate the side first, then the total, then the moneyline.
origination_order.why: The side and the total are the primitives; a moneyline is a function of the same distribution. Deriving the moneyline last keeps one distribution behind all three markets so they cannot disagree with each other.
origination_order.consequence_if_violated: Three independently fitted markets can imply three different games, and the disagreement is invisible until a parlay prices it.

output_contract.rule: Every model output is stored as a probability plus its inputs, never as a pick alone.
output_contract.why_the_inputs_are_stored: A pick without its inputs cannot be audited, cannot be re-run after a data correction, and cannot be asked what it would have said under a different availability state.
output_contract.two_sided_field: The brief asks for a two-sided 'what would change our mind' entry. Both directions are required: evidence that would strengthen the strategy and evidence that would kill it. A one-sided entry is a sales pitch, and the builder rejects it.

publication_columns.rule: Publish the model's fair line, the market line and the difference as three separate columns.
publication_columns.why_separate: A single 'edge' column hides which of the two inputs moved. A widening difference caused by the market moving is a different decision from one caused by our model moving.

total_estimators.rule: Publish every model total twice until one wins.

estimators.name: Team-total additive
estimators.description: Model each team's scoring distribution separately from its own inputs, then add them, so the total inherits both teams' availability and pace context.

estimators.name: Direct game-total
estimators.description: Model the combined game total directly from game-level features, so it can learn interaction effects that two independent team models cannot see.

total_estimators.gap_column: Both totals are published with a gap column (TOT-A minus TOT-B) on every row.
total_estimators.collapse_rule: Collapse to one estimator only after a pre-registered walk-forward comparison on the validation window, with the comparison and its interval published. Collapsing because one estimator looks better this month is fitting to noise.

ablations.rule: Injury and personnel effects are measured by ablation, never by subtracting a fixed number of points for a missing starter.
design: 1. Fit the identical model twice on the identical training window: once with the availability/personnel feature set, once without it.
2. Evaluate both on chronological holdouts, never on a random split, so no fold trains on the future.
3. Report the difference in the proper score, with an interval from a game-clustered bootstrap.
4. If the interval contains zero, the correct published statement is 'no measured effect at this sample size', not a point estimate.
ablations.why_not_fixed_penalties: A fixed penalty is a guess wearing a number. It cannot be falsified, it does not vary by position or by the quality of the replacement, and it silently becomes a permanent prior once it is in the code.
ablations.status: Protocol published. 0 ablations run, because verified availability features do not exist yet (Q-DEPTH-01).

injury_signal_form.rule: The injury signal is a surprise, never a level.
injury_signal_form.definition: surprise = designation observed at time t minus the expected designation for that player in that game week, where the expectation is built only from observations made strictly before t.
injury_signal_form.why_a_level_fails: A level says 'this player is Questionable'. A surprise says 'this player is Questionable when we expected him to be a full participant'. Only the second is new information, and only the second is not already priced by anyone reading the same report.
injury_signal_form.status: Definition published. 0 surprise values are computable from a single capture (Q-SNAPSHOT-01).

fixture_context_features.rule: Built only from published schedule facts - nothing inferred about form, motivation or travel fatigue.

fields.status: captured for 14 of 14 week 10 fixtures; 0 prior weeks
computable, published as derived and labelled as such

fixture_context_features.excluded: Anything not printed on the official schedule or game centre: no inferred travel fatigue, no timezone-adjustment model, no altitude or turf claim beyond the transcribed stadium name.

regime_priors.rule: 2026 kickoff and declared onside-kick regime priors must be estimated from 2026 results only.

confirmed_official_basis.text: Modifies alignment requirements for receiving team players in the setup zone on a kickoff or safety kick.
Modifies the dead ball spot after a touchback when the kickoff is from the 50-yard line.
Permits the kicking team to declare an onside kick at any time during the game.

Permits League personnel to consult with on-field officials when considering the potential disqualification of a player for both flagrant football and non-football acts, even if not called on the field.

regime_priors.why_null: The regime is confirmed; the rates under it are not measured. No pre-2026 rate is carried into a 2026 model, because rule 6-1-6 changes the onside-kick decision itself and mixing regimes biases totals and fourth-quarter comeback curves in one direction.
regime_priors.measurement_plan: Measure from official 2026 results only, publish n with each rate, and use wider intervals until n is large enough to narrow them.

weather_features.rule: Stadium roof/surface plus NWS hourly wind and precipitation, per kickoff.
weather_features.why_blank: The official per-game roof designation source was not located this session, so the field is blank and flagged (L-F-07) rather than assumed. Assuming 'outdoor' is the mispricing this requirement exists to prevent.

data_split.limitation: This is a within-season split because only the 2026 season has been captured. Roster context and the 2026 kickoff regime leak across folds. The season-level split the requirement asks for needs prior seasons (Q-MODEL-05).
data_split.holdout_discipline: The holdout is used once. Any use of holdout results to choose a model converts it into a validation set.
